Separately, Florida’s Attorney General sued Pfizer and its CEO over alleged misleading claims about the company’s COVID-19 vaccine. Meanwhile, the CDC now recommends COVID-19 vaccination for all adults and many children, and U.S. health groups and states have issued updated flu, COVID-19, and RSV vaccine guidance for the 2026-27 season. Additionally, CMS is reportedly considering ending certain COVID-19 data-reporting requirements for long-term care facilities.

news.headline: Invivyd Announces Positive Topline Results from LIBERTY Phase 3 Study Demonstrating VYD2311 Safety and Tolerability Superior to mRNA-based COVID-19 Vaccine; Announces Regulatory Submission Plans for VYD2311
news.body: VYD2311 met all primary and secondary endpoints comparing VYD2311 to an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, demonstrating VYD2311 safety and tolerability that is clinically and statistically superior to the safety and tolerability of an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccineVYD2311 combined with an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine demonstrated no interference with vaccine-induced neutralizing titers, and instead added substantially to vaccine-induced neutralizing titersVYD2311 observed profile in LIBERTY indicates high measured neutralizing antiviral titers supporting the target profile for VYD2311 under study in the DECLARATION pivotal clinical studyInvivyd plans for DECLARATION and LIBERTY clinical studies to be the basis of a planned Biologics License Application (BLA) submission for VYD2311 to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration via Accelerated Approval Program following a recent Type C meeting; DECLARATION topline data on safety and immunogenicity to support the submission are now expected in October; DECLARATION clinical efficacy data will be planned to be unblinded post-Accelerated Approval, if granted, subject to clinical event accrual Investor call to be held at 8:30 am ET on September 29, 2026 NEW HAVEN, Conn., Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Invivyd, Inc. (Nasdaq: IVVD) today announced positive, clinically meaningful, and statistically significant topline data from the LIBERTY Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active controlled study evaluating the safety and tolerability of (1) VYD2311, Invivyd’s investigational COVID-directed monoclonal antibody candidate, (2) mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine COMIRNATY® (mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, or COVID vaccine), and (3) VYD2311 co-administered with mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. The study also evaluated the potential for immunologic interference between VYD2311 and mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. LIBERTY is a companion study to DECLARATION, the ongoing placebo-controlled pivotal study of VYD2311 for pre-exposure prophylaxis of symptomatic COVID-19.

logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. logs.summary:
DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 8,000 confirmed cases amid a shortage of health workers, while the Africa CDC chief says contact tracing is falling far short, with only about 30,000 exposed people identified. Save the Children reports 961 children have died—about seven per day on average—with under-fives at greatest risk. Separately, NanoViricides has begun enrollment and dosing in a Phase II clinical trial of the oral drug NV-387 to treat Ebola.
Government figures show the DR Congo Ebola outbreak has now killed more than 4,000 people, making it the deadliest and fastest-growing outbreak on record. In a separate development, a fire destroyed a key Ebola transit centre in Ituri as fighting and displacement disrupted response efforts. Additionally, Island Pharmaceuticals has begun manufacturing the antiviral Galidesivir for an investigational Ebola treatment program.

incidents.summary:
Conway, Arkansas implemented Phase Three water restrictions, halting lawn and landscape irrigation due to drought. Bedford County, Virginia asked residents to voluntarily conserve water as drought persists. Karnataka, India sought Rs 3,705 crore in central drought relief, while a report detailed the decimation of Colorado’s biggest reservoir and its effects on recreation and livelihoods.
Karnataka, India now has 217 of its 240 taluks hit by drought, with losses estimated up to ₹60,000 crore; the state has requested ₹7,142 crore from the central government, while Andhra Pradesh declared 388 mandals drought-hit. In Maharashtra's Latur district, farmers are cutting standing sugarcane to feed livestock amid a severe fodder shortage. The Arkansas Department of Transportation suspended seasonal mowing along roads due to elevated wildfire risks, and a separate report notes September 2026 was the hottest on record and one of the driest, compounding crop losses.

Germany's Rhine River remained low, threatening navigation, and the NFU warned of crop failures. Other reports highlighted severe drought in Wisconsin, reduced grain harvests in Germany, and the potential for a super El Niño affecting Latin America and Sri Lanka.

logs.summary:
New reports highlight continued drought impacts: European agriculture suffered $3.6 billion in losses from heatwave-driven drought, and most of England's staple crops are grown in drought-risk areas, raising food price fears. Elsewhere, UNICEF warned 25.8 million children in Latin America face El Niño-related drought/flood risks, and the Philippines' Pagasa warned of a potential water crisis in Western Visayas due to below-normal rainfall expected through March 2027. In the U.S., central North Carolina saw no drought improvement after a dry week, while a separate study noted that Northeast drought has decreased in recent decades due to increased extreme precipitation.
Severe drought in Custer County, South Dakota, has forced Custer State Park to auction 612 bison to reduce its winter herd due to scarce forage. North Dakota's Drought Disaster Livestock Relief program exhausted its $4.1 million in funding after supporting 470 projects, as most of the state remains in drought. Meanwhile, September rains from a nor'easter brought broad improvements to drought conditions across Massachusetts and New England, according to the latest U.S. Drought Monitor.

logs.summary:
Conway, Arkansas implemented Phase Three water restrictions, halting lawn and landscape irrigation due to drought. Bedford County, Virginia asked residents to voluntarily conserve water as drought persists. Karnataka, India sought Rs 3,705 crore in central drought relief, while a report detailed the decimation of Colorado’s biggest reservoir and its effects on recreation and livelihoods.
Karnataka, India now has 217 of its 240 taluks hit by drought, with losses estimated up to ₹60,000 crore; the state has requested ₹7,142 crore from the central government, while Andhra Pradesh declared 388 mandals drought-hit. In Maharashtra's Latur district, farmers are cutting standing sugarcane to feed livestock amid a severe fodder shortage. The Arkansas Department of Transportation suspended seasonal mowing along roads due to elevated wildfire risks, and a separate report notes September 2026 was the hottest on record and one of the driest, compounding crop losses.

logs.summary: Two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela, causing widespread devastation. Death toll reports vary, with some sources citing at least 188 killed and others reporting over 3,800 deaths, while more than 68,000 people remain missing. Survivors face water shortages, and international aid and domestic relief efforts are underway.

logs.summary: Three months after the twin earthquakes, family members and volunteers continue searching collapsed buildings for their missing loved ones, with at least 1,500 people still unaccounted for. Separately, New Zealand engineers who traveled to Venezuela to assist in the aftermath are sharing lessons on earthquake resilience, highlighting that nearly 200 buildings collapsed and more than 16,000 structures were deemed unsafe.

news.headline: Kiwi engineers learn from Venezuela's devastating earthquakes
news.body: Last month, four New Zealand engineers flew to Venezuela to help in the aftermath of the devastating double quakes, which hit the western and central parts of the country in June, leaving more than 6000 people dead. Nearly 200 buildings collapsed in the quakes while more than 16-thousand structures were deemed unsafe. For the Kiwi engineers, it was a chance to learn about what New Zealand could do better, when it comes to earthquake resilience. University of Canterbury civil and environmental engineering Professor Santiago Pujol, director of the earthquake research centre, QuakeCore spoke to Ingrid Hipkiss.

logs.summary:
Ukraine struck additional warehouses of Russia's top online retailer Wildberries and intensified attacks on Ozon, causing economic disruption. In leadership moves, President Zelensky replaced the commander-in-chief with Mykhailo Drapatyi and fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sparking protests. Meanwhile, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russia's Lavrov in Manila, expressing readiness to help end the war but noting no quick deal is imminent.
Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries warehouses produced massive pillars of black smoke as fires raged at the facilities. Russia, stretched by Ukraine's drone attacks on its Black Sea Fleet, has pulled all warships from the Mediterranean Sea. Both sides have increased bridge strikes to disrupt resupply networks, indicating expectations of a prolonged stalemate, while the Kremlin warned against optimism on peace following the Rubio-Lavrov meeting.
The EU passed its 21st sanctions package with 218 new designations targeting Russia, including vessels that refuel shadow fleet tankers. Ukrainian strikes continued to hit Russian Wildberries warehouses, while new airstrikes caused deaths in both Ukraine and Russia, and a drone was shot down over NATO airspace.

Mediators persist amid Trump's rejection of Tehran's latest offer, as top aides meet at Camp David to discuss Iran and Yemen and Saudi Arabia plans an offensive against Houthis to break the Red Sea chokehold. logs.summary:
The U.S. and Iran have paused attacks and resumed diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, with mediators reporting progress and talks focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, the Pentagon quietly removed four recent troop deaths from its official Iran war death toll, reclassifying them in a new category, sparking controversy. Additional concerns include the U.S.'s dangerously low weaponry supply and growing public skepticism over the war’s costs and duration.
Mediators reported that neither the U.S. nor Iran conducted any attacks for three consecutive days, signaling progress in ceasefire efforts. New polls indicate that only one in three Americans now support the war, the lowest reading since the conflict began, and a majority view it as going "very badly." The Pentagon continued to face scrutiny over its reclassification of four troop deaths from the conflict.

logs.summary:
Diplomatic efforts collapsed as Secretary Rubio expelled Iran's delegation and Trump rejected Tehran's latest peace offer, warning he may resume bombing while sending a third aircraft carrier and 9,000 additional troops to the Mideast. Iran's currency hit a record low amid the war's economic toll, and the Pentagon announced higher combat pay, reporting 19 U.S. deaths and over 860 wounded. Other incidents included Iran claiming to capture a U.S. Navy drone, a FlyDubai copilot allegedly attempting to crash a Tel Aviv-bound flight, and new economic strain on U.S. farmers and Egypt aid.
The U.S. is sending a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the Middle East as Trump weighs new strikes on Iran. Trump threatened to hit Iran "very hard" if linked to the FlyDubai attack and cited Iran's "drug factories" as potential targets, while the Treasury announced new sanctions on Tehran's automotive and rail industries. Economic fallout continued as Northern Ireland diesel prices hit their highest level since the war began and analysts warned fuel subsidies could cost governments $1 trillion this year.

A new investigation reveals the U.S. bombing of a school in Minab killed over 120 children, drawing fresh war crimes allegations. Saudi Arabia is planning strikes against Houthis to secure Red Sea shipping lanes, while Italy warns the EU naval mission remains insufficient. Political fallout widens as a Maine Republican breaks with Trump, and economic impacts deepen with OPEC+ delaying capacity review and fuel subsidies projected to top $1 trillion.
The U.S. is expanding its military presence, dispatching up to 10,000 additional troops and weighing new strikes on Iran, while Iran warns of "painful" retaliation. news.headline: “The School That Became a Grave”: Jeremy Scahill on U.S Bombing of Minab, Killing 120+ Iranian Kids
news.body: Drop Site News released a major investigation this week into the U.S. bombing of the Shajareh Tayyebeh children’s school in the Iranian city of Minab on February 28, the first day of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Drop Site spoke to survivors, first responders, parents and witnesses in one of the most in-depth reports on the massacre to date. The bombing killed at least 156 people — 120 of the victims were children, 26 were teachers, and the rest were parents. A United Nations fact-finding mission recently concluded that the U.S. strike was a war crime, but the Trump administration has not yet even acknowledged U.S. responsibility. “This was not a single bombing or collateral damage,” says Drop Site News’s Jeremy Scahill, lead author of the investigation. “There were at least two direct hits on a school packed with children … and a couple of hours after those initial hits, as first responders came, as parents came, the U.S. launches more strikes.” Scahill points out that until 2013, the area where the school is was a facility operated by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps. But in satellite photos from just weeks before the strike, “You could see the murals on the wall. You could see the soccer field. Some of the satellite photos show shadows of tiny people playing outside.”

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
Rocky Mount, Virginia issued a voluntary water conservation request due to ongoing drought conditions, with the town receiving only about half its normal rainfall. In North Dakota, dry weather has caused hay shortages, with drought-damaged cereal crops down to 50% of normal, prompting producers to plan late-season alfalfa management. Separately, forecasters warn that the 2026-27 El Niño is strengthening into a very strong event, increasing the risk of heat and erratic rainfall.
Recent reports show drought persisting across several regions: central Minnesota's drought held steady while statewide conditions eased slightly, and eastern Idaho farmers are expecting lower potato yields due to drought and heat. Alabama's drought has been increasing, especially in southern and western areas, while St. Thomas has deteriorated into exceptional drought even as Puerto Rico saw slight improvement. Forecasts warn of a potentially unprecedented El Niño in 2026/27 that could bring below-normal rainfall to South Africa, and drought combined with the Black Sea grain crisis is raising global food security concerns, while El Niño-driven drought in Papua New Guinea has forced school sports cancellations.

logs.summary: Severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, and flash flooding impacted multiple regions across the United States from August 20–24, 2026. Confirmed tornadoes struck in Atlantic Beach (Long Island), Dover (Delaware), and York/Lancaster counties (Pennsylvania), while prolonged power outages from earlier storms left thousands without electricity in Gary, Indiana, for over a week. Widespread damage from downed trees, damaged homes, and flooding was reported in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Southeast, and Midwest.

logs.summary: A glacier collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border triggered devastating flash floods and mudslides on August 26, 2026, sweeping through several communities in the Bagmati region. The disaster has killed hundreds of people (with death tolls reported between 350 and 500) and left over 1,300 missing, including dozens of foreign nationals. Rescue teams are searching for survivors while authorities warn of additional flood risks from a newly formed lake, and international aid is arriving to support relief efforts.

news.headline: Aug. 27: Flash Flooding Overwhelms Nepal, and Jury Deliberates in Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Trial
news.body: Devastating flash floods and mudslides wreaked havoc along the Nepal-China border this week, leaving hundreds dead and more than 1,000 missing. More than 500 foreigners are among the missing, including, by one estimate, roughly 65 Americans. NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer explains why the destruction happened without warning and what role climate change may have played. Then, jury deliberations are underway in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children. While Clancy doesn’t dispute the killings, her defense team is arguing that she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. But the prosecution insists she acted intentionally and deliberately. As the jury weighs a set of complex outcomes, NBC News legal analyst Misty Marris breaks down what evidence and testimony from the five-week trial could be key to reaching a verdict. Finally, 2026 could be the year of the foldable phone. Samsung and Google already have models on the market, and Apple is reportedly planning to drop its version in September. But are consumers willing to shell out $2,000 for a little extra screen? NBC News chief tech analyst Joanna Stern explains why the phones have appeal.

news.headline: Fact Check: क्या पानी के तेज बहाव में बहती गाड़ियों का यह वीडियो नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा का है?
news.body: सोशल मीडिया पर नेपाल और थाईलैंड में आई बाढ़ से जोड़कर दो अलग-अलग वीडियो तेजी से वायरल हो रहे हैं. पहले वीडियो में पानी के तेज बहाव में गाड़ियों के बहने का दृश्य दिखाकर दावा किया गया कि यह नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर आई बाढ़ का है. पड़ताल के दौरान वीडियो में गाड़ियों के अप्राकृतिक तरीके से तैरने और धुंधली नंबर प्लेट जैसी खामियां मिलीं. एआई डिटेक्शन टूल्स की जांच में यह वीडियो 80 से 89 प्रतिशत तक एआई जनरेटेड पाया गया. वहीं दूसरे वीडियो में थाईलैंड की राजधानी बैंकॉक में बाढ़ के पानी में सड़कों पर मछलियों के तैरने का दावा किया गया. जांच में सुविधा स्टोर के साइन बोर्ड पर गलत वर्तनी, पानी की कम गहराई और स्थिर गाड़ियां दिखाई दीं. एआई डिटेक्शन टूल ने 97 प्रतिशत संभावना के साथ इसे भी एआई जनरेटेड बताया. इस तरह दोनों वायरल दावे पूरी तरह भ्रामक और फर्जी साबित हुए.

logs.summary:
On September 3, 2026, two Palestinian teens were killed in the occupied West Bank as Israeli settlers and snipers surrounded a village. Israeli forces bulldozed olive trees in the West Bank, while Prime Minister Netanyahu signaled plans to expand Israeli control over Gaza and the defence minister stated Israel still wants to remove Palestinians from Gaza. Additionally, a Gaza doctor continues to suffer torture in Israeli prison, and broader regional tensions escalated with Iranian missile and drone attacks targeting Kuwait.
On September 4, 2026, the UN raised 'ethnic cleansing' concerns over Israel's West Bank operation, reporting over 33,000 Palestinian refugees still displaced. Israeli police killed a Palestinian in Jerusalem after an alleged knife attack. Meanwhile, far-right minister Ben-Gvir outlined a plan for the forced expulsion of all Palestinians from Gaza.

logs.summary: Severe monsoon rains and cyclones have caused widespread flooding across the Philippines, particularly in Luzon, with damage nearing P4 billion in Central Luzon and P2.68 billion in infrastructure damage in the Ilocos Region, affecting over four million people. At least two brothers drowned in a submerged bypass road in Pampanga, and a baby was dramatically rescued from flash floods in Manila. In response, lawmakers are pushing for flood control master plan reviews and Senate investigations into the government's disaster response.

The Joint Typhoon Warning Center classifies it as Tropical Cyclone 01B, while the India Meteorological Department officially considers it a deep depression; social media erroneously named it "Cyclone Arnab". Red alerts and heavy rain warnings are in place for the affected areas.
